issues.legal_issue: Interest awarded on a refunded payment for the period it was withheld is income rather than a capital receipt.
material_facts: Authorities collected estate duty that was later held not payable and directed to be refunded.
The court ordering the refund also awarded legal interest from the institution of the proceedings.
The assessee received a share of that interest through the distribution of the estate.
issues.conclusion: The interest received by the assessee was income liable to tax, not a capital receipt in the nature of damages for wrongful retention of money.
issues.legal_principle: The court applied the natural meaning of “interest” in section 192 of the Ceylon Civil Procedure Ordinance, 1889, which distinguishes interest from the principal sum adjudged. Interest compensating for deprivation of the use of money has the quality of income even if it may also be described as damages. The court relied on Westminster Bank Ltd. v. Riches and followed Dr. Shamlal Narula v. Commissioner of Income-tax, which held that statutory interest for delayed payment was a revenue receipt.

predicates.income_tax_assessment: The receipt was considered in an income-tax assessment.
predicates.court_awarded_interest_on_refunded_money: A court ordered money that had been collected but was not payable to be refunded, together with interest.
predicates.interest_compensated_for_withheld_money: The awarded interest compensated the recipient for being deprived of the use of the money.

issues.definition: When an income-tax assessment concerns court-awarded interest compensating for withheld money ordered to be refunded, the interest receipt is taxable income.

issues.legal_issue: Interest that accrues over time and is anticipated is not a casual and non-recurring receipt merely because it is paid as a lump sum.
material_facts: The interest was awarded from the date proceedings were instituted and was calculated as accruing day by day.
When the proceedings began, the claimants could anticipate that a successful outcome would result in interest as well as repayment.
The interest was ultimately paid as a lump sum.
issues.conclusion: The interest receipt was not exempt as a receipt of a casual and non-recurring nature.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 4(3)(vii) of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, qualifying casual and non-recurring receipts were excluded from total income. A lump-sum payment can nevertheless have the quality of recurrence when the interest accrues day by day. A receipt that is foreseen and anticipated is not casual merely because it is unlikely to recur.

predicates.income_tax_assessment: The receipt was considered in an income-tax assessment.
predicates.interest_accrued_over_time: The interest was calculated as accruing over time during the period for which money was withheld.
predicates.interest_was_anticipated: The claimants could anticipate when proceedings began that a successful outcome would include interest.

issues.definition: In an income-tax assessment, interest that accrued over time and was anticipated is not exempt as casual and non-recurring.

issues.legal_issue: A High Court deciding a tax reference may decide only questions referred to it or arising from the Tribunal's order.
material_facts: In a tax reference, the assessee argued that its share of the interest was received as part of the estate and was therefore capital.
That argument had not been raised before or decided by the Tribunal, and the question had not been referred to the High Court.
issues.conclusion: The High Court could not decide the assessee's un-referred argument that the receipt was capital as part of the estate.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 66 of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, the High Court acts in an advisory capacity on a reference and may decide only questions referred to it or arising out of the Tribunal's order. The court followed Commissioner of Income-tax, Bombay v. Scindia Steam Navigation Co. Ltd.

rule.if: tax_reference_proceeding and not issue_referred and not issue_arose_from_tribunal_order

predicates.tax_reference_proceeding: The matter came before the High Court as a reference from an income-tax Tribunal.
predicates.issue_referred: The question the party asks the High Court to decide was referred to it.
predicates.issue_arose_from_tribunal_order: The question the party asks the High Court to decide arose from the Tribunal's order.

issues.definition: In a tax reference, when an issue was neither referred nor arose from the Tribunal's order, the High Court must not decide it.
